annotations.title: Deadline After Service (Your Rule's Days, Mail Days, Rollover)

description: Count a deadline that runs a number of days after service, using the numbers your court rule or statute states (state court, agency, arbitration, or a court order). Send the service date, the period in days (calendar or court days), the days your rule adds for the service method (mail, electronic, overnight), whether those days are added after the period's last day has been moved off a weekend or holiday (the federal Rule 6(d) way) or counted on together with the period before any move, and the holidays your court closes on. U.S. federal holidays (on their observed days) are built in and can be turned off. Get back the deadline, its weekday, every day skipped and why, and each step of the count. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/docket-days-rule). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

added_count_in.description: Whether the added days are calendar_days (default) or court_days, as your rule says.

added_days.description: Days your rule adds for how the paper was served (for example 3 under the federal rule for mail; your state's number for mail or electronic service). 0 if none.

added_days_when.description: after_rollover (default; Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(d)): find the period's deadline first, moving it off a weekend or holiday, then add the days. with_period: add the days straight on from the period's last day, then move the result once.

count_in.description: calendar_days (default): every day counts. court_days: only days that are not a Saturday, Sunday or holiday count.

days.description: The period your rule states, in days (10, 14, 20, 21, 30 ...).

holidays.description: Other days your court is closed or your rule calls holidays (state holidays, the day after Thanksgiving, closures), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 60).

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'response to motion' (your own text, echoed; not a party name).

rollover.description: forward (default): a last day on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday moves to the next day that is not one. none: no move (only if your rule says so).

rule_cited.description: Optional: the rule you are applying, e.g. 'Tex. R. Civ. P. 21a' (your own text, echoed; it is not read or checked).

service_date.description: Date of service (the day that starts the count; it is not counted), YYYY-MM-DD.

us_federal_holidays.description: Count the 11 U.S. federal holidays, on the days federal offices observe them, as holidays (default true). Set false for a court that does not close on them, and send its holidays instead.
